title: Idioms
content:
Definition

English: Idioms are fixed expressions or phrases whose meanings are different from the meanings of the individual words.
Hindi: Muhavare (Idioms) aise sthir vakyaansh hote hain jinka arth pratyek shabd ke arth se alag hota hai.

They express ideas or emotions in a colorful and creative way.
Yeh bhavnaon aur vicharon ko rochak aur prabhavshali tarike se vyakt karte hain.

Example: “Break the ice” means to start a conversation.
Hindi: “Break the ice” ka arth hai baatcheet shuru karna.

title: Features of Idioms
content:
Explanation

English: Idioms are commonly used expressions whose meaning cannot be understood literally.
Hindi: Muhavaron ka arth seedha nahi samjha ja sakta, ve vaakya ke sandarbh se arth dete hain.

  • Fixed in form (cannot be changed).
  • Figurative meaning, not literal.
  • Often cultural or contextual.
  • Add color and naturalness to speech.
Example: “Under the weather” means 'feeling sick'.
Hindi: “Under the weather” ka arth hai 'bimar hona'.

title: Common English Idioms
content:
Popular Examples

  • A piece of cake: Very easy. / Hindi: बहुत आसान।
  • Break the ice: Start a conversation. / Hindi: बातचीत शुरू करना।
  • Hit the sack: Go to sleep. / Hindi: सोने जाना।
  • Under the weather: Feeling ill. / Hindi: बीमार महसूस करना।
  • Spill the beans: Reveal a secret. / Hindi: राज खोल देना।
  • Once in a blue moon: Very rarely. / Hindi: बहुत कम।
  • Cost an arm and a leg: Very expensive. / Hindi: बहुत महंगा।
  • Beat around the bush: Avoid the main topic. / Hindi: घुमा-फिरा कर बात करना।
  • Let the cat out of the bag: Leak a secret. / Hindi: राज उगल देना।
  • Time flies: Time passes quickly. / Hindi: समय तेजी से बीतता है।

title: Common Hindi Idioms
content:
Popular Hindi Idioms

  • ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा: A very small amount compared to need. / English: A drop in the ocean.
  • हाथ पर हाथ धरे बैठना: Sit idle. / English: Do nothing.
  • दूध का जला छाछ भी फूंक-फूंक कर पीता है: Once bitten, twice shy. / English: Be cautious after a bad experience.
  • नाक में दम करना: Keep bothering someone. / English: To annoy someone constantly.
  • आसमान से गिरे खजूर में अटके: Out of the frying pan into the fire. / English: One trouble after another.
  • नाक कटना: To lose respect. / English: To feel ashamed.
  • नाकों चने चबवाना: To trouble someone badly. / English: To make someone struggle.

title: Idioms by Category
content:
Grouped by Themes

English: Idioms can be grouped according to topics such as emotions, time, work, etc.
Hindi: Muhavare vishayon ke anusaar vibhaajit kiye ja sakte hain jaise bhavna, samay, ya kaam se sambandhit.

  • Time idioms: At the eleventh hour (antim samay par)
  • Work idioms: By the book (niyamon ke anusaar)
  • Emotion idioms: All ears (dhyaan se sunna)
  • Luck idioms: Break a leg (good luck)
  • Difficulty idioms: A hard nut to crack (muskhil samasya)

title: Importance of Idioms
content:
Use

English: Idioms enrich your language, making communication more natural and expressive.
Hindi: Muhavare aapki bhasha ko samriddh aur prabhavshali banate hain.

They help learners sound fluent and native-like.
Yeh seekhne walon ko prakritik aur pravahmay bolne mein madad karte hain.

title: Common Challenges
content:
Explanation

English: Idioms can be confusing because their meanings aren’t literal.
Hindi: Muhavare kathin lagte hain kyunki unka arth seedha nahi hota.

Example: 'Kick the bucket' doesn’t mean literally kicking; it means 'to die'.
Hindi: 'Kick the bucket' ka arth 'marna' hota hai, na ki 'balti marna'.

title: How to Learn Idioms
content:
Tips

  • Learn by theme (e.g., time, emotion, work).
  • Use idioms in writing and daily speech.
  • Make flashcards with Hindi meanings.
  • Understand context — don’t translate literally.
Example: Practice sentences like 'It’s a piece of cake' to express ease.
